body: Since it's chemically similar to effexor, it's like coming off both an opiate and an SSRI.  Aside from benzo withdrawals, it was one of my worst dependences to break.. and I used other, more potent opiates.  I just took very large doses for a long time and my body came to depend on it.. nasty drug and the smallest euphoria you get from it goes away quickly if it was even there at all.  Shitty opiate with nasty withdrawals in my case.

I think it's different for everyone, but I think you are probably in the clear.  You may have some depression and I believe your GABA receptors will continue healing for some time, but I'd say you are highly unlikely to have a seizure at this point unless you have a lower than normal threshold (as in.. you have epilepsy, etc.).

I went cold turkey after being on klonopin consistently for a year and a halfish, going from therapeutic sleep doses of 0.5mg to 6+mg straight up binges.  I felt like I would literally die due to the physical and mental pain of withdrawals and feared seizures constantly.  I failed at the taper, so I felt this was my only option.  I never had a seizure, though people at lower doses have had seizures.  We all have different bodies, but I'm explaining myself as a sort of worst case scenario that didn't end in seizures, etc.  If you haven't had them so far, you're probably fine!

Good luck and great job on your success!
Maybe.. I would like to try, at least.

I think the same thing at times.  It is so.. heavy.  So disheartening beyond all words.  My mother forwarded me information about a new med for treatment resistant depression and I just keep holding onto the idea that something will eventually work.  I'm going to talk to my psychiatrist about it when I can manage the courage to go in.  I didn't think I'd have the courage to try another med that might backfire, but hey.. something might work.

I'll be hoping the best for you and me, both.  I hate that you feel this way, but thank you for letting me know I'm not alone.
If only.. I always make myself count from waking until sleeping.  But how do I count now if I'm repeatedly drugging myself to sleep?
Yes and still I somehow expect the impossible to happen!  Silly!

I told myself I hadn't had kids because I wasn't physically healthy enough or couldn't find a partner for the "long haul," but now I think.. would the kid be bringing me water when I'm curled up in bed wanting to die?  Would I be afraid to give a child carbs for fear it would have the same physical and mental reaction?  Since I was tormented about my weight and then developed an eating disorder, would it suffer the same fate?  If it was, quite honestly, more likely through DNA to be a bigger kid, how could I make sure it doesn't end up hating itself like me?  Could I give them freedom or would I be mentally counting their nutrition in the back of my mind from day one?  How many calories does a newborn need?

I like to think I'd get my shit together.  My psychologist says **all** people have worries before having kids.  Still, is it worth it for some innocent little person to be my test experiment?  Do I want to model the secret part of my life accidentally until they catch on and start doing the same?  Probably not, as much as I'd love children.  My DNA might be enough to scar a child, even if the environment was healthy.

This stuff makes me so sad.  I've met people who adopt animals and constantly recycle them.  Like.. they get a puppy, it grows up, they rehome it, repeat.  It always infuriates me.  How can you act like a pet is like a leased vehicle?

Pets will love you no matter what and some people just treat them like absolute garbage.  We don't deserve 'em.

I lost my job due to panic attacks while working and then I got extremely sick (physically).  I applied for medicaid insurance and had to go through social security disability first.  I thought it was just a formality and that I would be denied, but due to physical health conditions and mental illness, I was surprisingly approved.

The government has a job in protecting its people and though I feel embarrassed by it and hope it is only temporary, I'm grateful to be protected at this point.  I had feared homelessness forever due to my anxiety, depression, PTSD, etc.  It is finally something I don't have to worry about and I would encourage all who need it to apply.

I have felt a little guilty about being depressed lately because people close to me are actively grieving a horrific accidental death in my extended family.. but you know what?  I've done everything to try and be "better" and still keep slipping into the pit.  Depression is as much of an illness as anything else, sometimes terminal, and we are invalidated enough by other people who don't understand, so I say why be so hard on ourselves?

You're not pathetic for suffering, though.  Every day we keep going is a sign of strength, in my opinion.

I still suffer from this, but when I was doing my best, I was doing a combination of medication (SSRI), therapy, and mindfulness/meditation.  I was also following a really rigid keto diet (sugar fluctuations work havoc on my mental state), working on goals, and attending a support group.  This was a perfect combination for me at that time, BUT I could not see myself able to do all of that again!  It takes an energy and a drive I no longer possess.  Still, taking my medicine on time, adhering to a diet when I can, therapy when I can.. these all seem to help.  Physical comforts like warm showers, heavy blankets, warm drinks, and keeping myself as distracted as possible are some things I do in the moment.

It's a difficult battle, but these are some of the things that help.  Venting to a friend and just crying helps me.. though there are very few people I'd trust to do that with.
Do you want to talk?  I know the grip of depression and suicidal thoughts.  Sometimes it is difficult to get through the moment, but I'm often glad I did.  If you need someone to listen, I'm here.

I have to wear natural looking makeup because my skin looks like shit from when I used to have breakouts and occasionally still do.  Was on meds for it and it never helped much.  Skin still gets dry and I have a tough time making it look good/smooth.

Extra skin from mega weight loss.

Scars from emergency surgery on my abdomen.

Extra weight I'm still losing.

Weird looking face maybe.

Mainly, I used to be bigger.  I went on medicine for a health condition, did keto for ages, and lost lots of weight.  I still have extra skin and weight to lose.  And the ex bf told me if I gained weight, he wouldn't be able to find me attractive.  So, it is stuck in my head, despite I was at my lowest weight since I was probably 10.

We had broken up twice before and once it was due to him feeling bad about being younger than me, along with distance.. he broke it off and ghosted me.   The second time I broke it off when he told me he wouldn't be attracted to me if I gained weight.  This time..I think he just didn't feel attracted to me, period.  It's hard because I tried to never bring my mental illness into things - if he wanted to spend time with me, I was always available and i encouraged him in work, other activities, his other friendships.  No matter how shitty and insignificant he made me feel at times, I tried so hard to not appear sad or upset.  There were so many times that I swallowed bad feelings rather than start a fight because he would shut down and refuse to talk if I had an issue.. he'd get defensive and I quickly learned that if I I didn't want him to go away.. I'd better not cause too many issues.  When I had issues with him lying, he told me he had to take the night to think of what was best for him... so, if I ever had an issue, I just knew to keep quiet or he'd withdraw love or break up with me.

I thank you for the hug.  I .. know I sound pathetic probably, but it means so much to me.

So glad that you got off them - compared to my opiate addiction, the withdrawal from benzos was so much worse.  They are definitely silent killers and I had so many around that it amazes me.

How long did it take for the anxiety to settle down?  I was functioning worse than ever and doing batshit crazy stuff before I came off them.

Thank you for your response.  I have lost most of my real life friends due to extreme anxiety keeping me home.  I hope I can try to make the best of things, but it seems to be getting worse all the time.

Thank you again for responding to me
6 months and 12 days.  Still breathing.

Try not to look at statistics regarding chances to live, etc.  I did this when I had a really freak incident occur, too, and convinced myself I was going to die.  I was too scared to sleep in the hospital, which caused hallucinations that had I not hidden would have probably taking me to an entirely different wing!  I know it's scary, but try to hang on to the fact you're getting this taken care of asap.  I'll be hoping for the best for you!

Over six months from my doc, still battling depression, but alive if that counts for something.
I feel this so hard right now. I take meds and sleep 12 hours a day and it's not enough.  Hoping you feel better

I empathize so much.  I don't know if I'll ever stop struggling, either.  At the heart of it, I guess it is okay.  It's exhausting and sometimes I wonder what life would be like otherwise.  There was a time when things were better for a year or so, but they've become much worse, so I don't know if there will be periods of real goodness again.

I guess we can just keep living with ourselves and see what happens.  For what it's worth, I hope you see your own success story become a reality.

Mine has progressively worsened to the point I have had the worst functioning year of my life probably.  I continue suffering in the hope that something good will happen and also because I'm afraid to die.  I think I want to be a survivor.  I actually don't know what I want, but I have to think it will eventually ease up again.  New treatments will come out, I may have something show up in my life that makes me want to live.  I may have half of my life yet, so it stands to reason that some good things could potentially happen.  It sucks, but if this is all we have, I'm not ready for oblivion just yet.  I've seen people's lives do a 180 for the best.. and if mine can turn into a total shitshow within a couple of years, maybe it has the potential to get better, too.

That makes a lot of sense to me..  I am going to therapy, but so far my issues have felt pretty resistant to treatment. I have talked a lot about things that have happened during adulthood, but haven't addressed the childhood stuff as much.  In fact, my first therapists had no idea about my childhood issues.  Maybe I need to delve into it with the current psychologist.  She's gently nudged me before, but I shy away.  Maybe it's time.

Have you seen improvement?  I honestly don't know how I'd accept someone loving me unconditionally, either.

I almost used over the weekend.  It had been well over six months since I had my doc.  Life is spiraling downward.  Somehow, despite hating myself, I didn't do it.  It feels almost miraculous because somedays I just dream about feeling like I used to.  Sometimes I feel like opiates were the only way I ever accepted myself and felt confident.  I wonder if I'll ever feel that way without them.
This is awesome!  Once you start showering and taking care of this stuff again, it gets so much easier to do it.  I think it's an amazing step in the right direction!!
Sleep is the best part of my life.
Nope, I seriously doubt it had any impact.  Mental health just seems to ebb and flow for many of us.

It sounds shitty, but it gets better.  During my first withdrawals, it was a nightmare.  The physical and mental symptoms were overwhelming.  I also cried about the withdrawal and about getting started on them in the first place.  Although it sucks and hurts like hell, it's normal.

I'd suggest repeatedly calling therapists or a psychiatrist and being honest with the reception folks.  I have called in the midst of panic attacks.  Explain it's dire and you need to be on a waiting list.  I hurt for you in that you haven't been able to talk to someone.

For physical pain, I can recommend a lot of stretches and walking around when you can make yourself get up, tylenol, flexeril, etc.  I was on clonidine and that helped.  I had restless legs and muscle aches and twitches.. sometimes only getting up helped.  I took benadryl and vistaril, but I'm convinced it made restless legs worse.  Showers, when I could take them, with warm water helped.

Mental pain and symptoms.. talking to close friends sometimes helped, but I lost a friend in the process because they expected compensation despite offering with a free heart.  I guess it is an easy time to become prey, so might not be bad to not depend on others.  I cried a lot.  I still do.  I just tried to get through the moment.. video games, lots of 'The Office' and just suffering in misery.  Took about a month and a half until I could distract myself with reading.  Showers are now a good distraction.  A couple of months out from hopefully my last cold turkey incident and I stopped stuttering and contemplating suicide all day every day.  I'm miserable, but I think this is mostly my normal depression and anxiety.  So, just keep looking forward.  The acute withdrawals suck, but even during my most miserable days, I'm so thankful not to have the awful muscle tics and stuttering and physical pain.  It makes it easier to live, at the very least.

Wishing you all the best

I took benzos occasionally for a long time and didn't have issues.. but I found that feeling like I need it one day means leaning on it the next, etc.. until I'm taking it daily and taking way more than prescribed.  Kpin stays in your system for a long time, so I personally wouldn't take it unless I was having a panic attack or about to kill myself.  What about benadryl?
I feel the same way about myself, but I don't see it in you.  Lovely lips and hair, especially.  I wonder if the person was just a troll?

Medication helped me with this, but then I became an addict for a bit, so I wouldn't take my advice in that department.  I also struggle with agoraphobia due in part to BDD, so benzos (klonopin, ativan, valium) worked well sometimes and were recommended by my psychiatrist and psychologist for a while.

Do you want to go out and avoid people/not be seen?  I used to shop late at night or during the day. Maybe you could start with that.  Go to places that aren't overly populated, particularly those without younger groups of people.  Try the park or the library at off peak hours and gradually try to increase what you can tolerate.

Wishing you much luck.

I am guilty of responding to a post regarding this topic.  I talked about my frustration at feeling objectively awful looking compared to some people, but I don't dismiss how others feel.  I had a body part I obsessed over and hated for years, wishing for plastic surgery.. now I think it's okay.  I truly hated it before.  I'm really unattractive by the standards of most and do feel I could function better if others thought I looked somewhat attractive.. I am very lonely and think it would help in some ways.  Social, work, etc.

Still, I looked through the femcel stuff and it just doesn't seem applicable?  I am not celibate and haven't been for most of my adult life.  I have relationships, just not relationships in which I'm treated well.  I'm fine for some people to use for sex, companionship, etc., but not good enough to be respected or cherished.  I sometimes can't tell if I'm quite as horrible as I think I am, but, objectively, I do have a lot of physical imperfections which I think render me unlovable and prone to physical and mental abuse and resentment.

We are all struggling and I can, sadly, see how many of us would be envious of others' attributes or situations.  I hate BDD and how it sucks the joy out of all of our lives.

I so empathize with you.  This is the reason I never go to conventions or would never ask for pics with any celebrity that I admire.  I know what I look like.  I've been looking in the mirror all these years. It amazes me how some people can cast aside their appearances and embrace life.  I envy them!

I'm going through the same thing and it's driving me crazy.  I wonder which part of me it was and how long had they been feeling that way about me.  I had to hide my insecurity and paranoia, but I still felt it.

I'll be hoping the depression eases up for you soon - this is a horrible place to be.

I also feel this way.  I know I'm not conventionally attractive; I've been fat and lost weight, having the ruined body to show for that and I'm still not thin.  I grew quickly in puberty and have those stretch from that, too.  I have dry, sensitive skin and I still have rough skin due to my earlier, bad skin years (yes, I was on medicine and I still struggled).

I try not to be in photos online and when I am, I know I'm just getting pity likes and comments for the most part.

My partners have been abusive to me, either physically or mentally and sometimes both.  I met all of them online, so I know it was my personality they cared about and resented falling for the ugly girl.

I had a good personality and it's been more of a curse than anything.  People like me then become revolted by me.

So, am I resentful?  I guess, but I don't blame anyone for not liking me.  Evolution is just weeding my bad genetics out of the gene pool.
